node.title: Re^4: Text::CSV encoding parse()
node.author: slugger415
node.doctext:
Hello, ok here's as short and succinct a sample as I can create.

use Text::CSV; use CGI; my($row) = "search/¿Cuales son las partes de una cadena de conexión??scope|ids_jdbc_011.htm|0|1|1|0"; my $csv = Text::CSV->new ({ binary => 1, sep_char => "|" }); my $q = new CGI; # print the HTML header and start html print $q->header; print $q->start_html; # first, print $row as is print $q->p("ROW: $row"); # next, parse with $csv $csv->parse($row); my @els = $csv->fields; # print the first field # this displays the black diamond ? symbol for ¿ and ó print $q->p("CSV Parse, field 0:",$els[0]); # split instead my(@splits) = split('\|',$row); # print the first element in @splits. # As noted, this one displays properly in the browser. print $q->p("split 0:", $splits[0]); print $q->end_html; exit;

thanks

======================
